answer.rationale: Current situation shows both activation and onboarding completion are down 4-6% QoQ, signaling friction in the funnel. Memory_31 and memory_86 establish that signup simplification and shortened onboarding both improved activation and time-to-value durably. Memory_73 shows promotional pricing works for price-sensitive segments, but we face a specific activation/onboarding degradation that predates the competitive threat—this is a product friction issue, not purely a pricing problem. Verifying memory_31 (SMB activation via field reduction) and memory_73 (promotional pricing efficacy) will confirm whether onboarding simplification remains a high-confidence lever and whether pricing alone is sufficient. Onboarding simplification addresses the root degradation directly and aligns with long-term qualified revenue by improving product-market fit signals. Enterprise_sales_assist is valuable but targets a different segment; referral_incentive works for existing customers, not acquisition. Standard_experiment scale allows confident measurement without overcommitting resources.
